title: Check yourself: The surfaces: one model behind many doors

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A marketing manager with no engineering support needs weekly newsletters drafted in the house voice, using last quarter's issues as reference. Which approach fits best?

options.text: A cloud-platform deployment so the drafts stay inside the company account
options.says: Ruled out because the cloud platforms row is for "Organisations that buy Claude through a cloud account", which the scenario never mentions.

options.text: A scheduled script that calls the Messages API weekly with the issues attached
options.says: Ruled out because "A recurring chat workflow for a non-developer does not need code".

options.text: A bespoke agent on the Agent SDK that reads the archive before each draft
options.says: Ruled out because the Agent SDK row is for "Developers building custom agents", and a Project already holds the archive without code.

options.text: A Project in the app holding the tone guide and earlier editions
options.says: A Project holds instructions and reference files for recurring non-developer work (the apps bullet and the first trap).

questions.stem: A bank must run every model call under the identity and permission setup of the cloud provider that already hosts its servers. Developers still want the same Claude models from their own code. Which option fits?

options.text: Install Claude Code on every laptop and share one settings file
options.says: Ruled out because the shared engine only means "your repo's CLAUDE.md files, settings, and MCP servers work across all of them", not that identity rules are enforced.

options.text: Order access through that vendor's matching platform listing
options.says: The table sends "Security requires all traffic through the company's cloud account" to a cloud platform, which adds its own identity and permission model while serving the same models.

options.text: Call the Messages API directly with rules in the system prompt
options.says: Ruled out because "a cloud platform adds its own identity and permission model", while a system prompt only instructs the model.

options.text: Create an app Project and write the rules into its instructions
options.says: Ruled out because "A Project's instructions do not reach the API", and the developers call the models from code.

questions.stem: A developer wrote "answer in French" into a Project's instructions. Their own integration, calling the Messages API, still replies in English. What is the best explanation?

options.text: The Messages API supports fewer languages than the apps do
options.says: Ruled out because "The model is the same family behind every door, so its capabilities and its quirks are the same".

options.text: The integration needs the Agent SDK before it can follow language rules
options.says: Ruled out because "Instructions written for one place do not appear in another unless you put them there", and no other surface is a precondition.

options.text: French must be requested through a model parameter that the API leaves unset
options.says: Ruled out because the instruction lives "In the API, in the system prompt your code sends", and no model parameter is involved.

options.text: Settings kept in the chat product are not sent with requests from code
options.says: Where instructions live decides where they are read, and a Project's instructions do not reach the API (the carry-across section and the third trap).
